notes: Table 3 (classification/novelty/WSD) and Table 5 (regression) compare the proposed asynchronous CUDA TM (Tesla V100) with single-core pyTsetlinMachine CPU TMs with and without clause indexing (Xeon Platinum 8168). Speed-ups are CUDA vs indexed. Table 4 timings (TM CUDA vs ThunderSVM) were run on Google Colab, GPU model not stated. Clause scope for BBC Sports (5,000) and 20 Newsgroup (10,000) is not stated (left not_reported). Bike Sharing settings T=1280, s=1.5, n=1280 are stated for Fig. 5/6; applied to Table 5 as an inference. Epoch counts only stated for the novelty-detection runs (100); Fig. 5/6 x-axes go to 100 epochs for Bike Sharing but this is not stated in text, so epochs left not_reported. No booleanization details for the regression or novelty datasets. Train/test split sizes not given for BBC, 20NG, SemEval, IMDb. The abstract says 'up to 50 times faster', while Table 5 reports 156.4x and 211.6x for the regression datasets. Figures 3, 4, 6-9 (MAE/time vs clauses/epochs) are curves without tabulated values and were not extracted. Sec. 4.5: up to 7,000 clauses and an extension to 15,000 clauses (Fig. 7, BBC Sports) with near-constant time. Table 5 ± values are called a 'confidence interval' in its caption (type not stated), unlike Table 3's standard deviations.
